title.narrative: Providing Multi-Purpose Cas Assistance, Critical Protection Services and Strengthened AAP and PSEA Measures for Communities Affected by Multiple Tropical Cyclones and Flooding

description.narrative: In response to the humanitarian needs identified during the typhoon season, UNICEF will implement cross-sectoral interventions to address the urgent needs of children and vulnerable families. This includes providing immediate cash assistance, strengthening child protection mechanisms, enhancing accountability to affected populations, and ensuring the prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA). These efforts are aligned with the Humanitarian Needs and Priorities (HNP) and coordinated with government and local partners to maximize reach and impact.Social ProtectionTo enable vulnerable and poor households with children to meet their essential needs during emergencies, UNICEF’s social protection in emergencies programming includes following actions:Provide multipurpose, unrestricted humanitarian cash transfers to 5,000 4Ps households in the hardest hit province of Catanduanes and CagayanConduct community sensitization and Cash Plus sessions to 5,000 4Ps households focusing on nutrition, child protection, WASH, F1KDConduct post distribution monitoring of the cash transfersChild ProtectionIn line with the priorities identified in the Revised HNP, Child Protection shall focus on the following priority actions: Establish and/or strengthen protection and referral pathways with mandated local structures such as Barangay Council for the Protection of Children (BCPC) and VAWC desks. Enhance community-level systems to address protection concerns, including violence against children (VAC) and family separation prevention and response. Coordination and facilitation of MHPSS sessions, for at least 2,000 children, adolescents and youth; and their caregivers. This include PFA and capacity building for service providers. Accountability to Affected PopulationTo enhance inclusive, transparent, and responsive humanitarian programming, UNICEF’s AAP initiatives focus on the following actions:Establish culturally appropriate and accessible feedback and complaint mechanisms in priority areas, such as feedback boxes, help desks, hotlines, and digital platforms, ensuring communities can voice concerns and receive timely responses.Conduct community engagement activities to promote awareness of services, entitlements, PSEA, and available feedback platforms, aligning with sectoral response efforts.Facilitate community consultations and rapid assessments to identify gaps in communication needs and feedback systems, ensuring marginalized groups are included in response planning and decision-making.Provide training for UNICEF staff, implementing partners, and community focal points on AAP tools, methodologies, and approaches, enhancing capacity for participatory and accountable programming.Monitor feedback trends and referral processes, ensuring the resolution of community concerns and the integration of insights into program adjustments.PSEATo enable vulnerable populations to access a safe and accessible channel for reporting sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA) by humanitarian, development, protection, or other personnel providing assistance to affected populations, the PSEA initiatives focus on the following:Review and update the reporting and referral mechanisms for SEA allegations.Ensure functionality, adherence to the zero-tolerance policy, and the provision of assistance and services for SEA survivors. This includes personnel, volunteers, and implementing partners, as well as the management and dissemination of reporting hotlines and other alternative mechanisms through PSEA orientations.Build the capacity of PSEA volunteers and advocates on the reporting and referral mechanisms for PSEA.
